verdict.rationale: Blaxel's own sandbox features address credential isolation: an outbound proxy can inject secrets via MITM header and body injection rather than placing them in the sandbox, and executed code can be scoped to an unprivileged user while the sandbox API keeps its privileges. The docs never state that host secrets or credentials are unreachable from sandboxed code, and the separate env-var/secrets feature puts secrets inside the sandbox. missing for 10: explicit documentation that injected credentials are invisible to sandbox code, a description of the isolation boundary (VM/microVM separation from host), independent or hands-on verification.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can give an agent a sandbox where host secrets and credentials are unreachable by the code it runs

citations.quote: Route outbound sandbox traffic through Blaxel's proxy with MITM header and body injection, inject secrets, and configure per-domain firewalls.
Scope everything a sandbox runs on your behalf to an unprivileged user while the sandbox API keeps the privileges it needs.
